Question: What indicators does our cardiac monitor use to show a STEMI alert?

Passages:
[1] 700-M09 4.9 (12-Lead Electrocardiogram): Procedure
4.9. ECG criteria for STEMI Alerts: Please note that depending on the manufacturer of the
cardiac monitor, STEMI indicators may vary. Is incumbent on the provider to know
what indicators your manufacturer uses. Most manufacturers demarcate STEMI’s with
three (3) asterisks before and after the text and use capitalized and bolded text.

reports shall start with a clear statement indicating what type of alert applies to the

transmit the 12 lead ECG to the STEMI receiving hospital

[4] 700-M09 4.9.1 (12-Lead Electrocardiogram): Procedure > ECG criteria for STEMI Alerts: Please note that depending on the manufacturer of the
4.9.1. If the ECG monitor reading identifies a STEMI:

[5] 700-M09 4.9.1.2 (12-Lead Electrocardiogram): Procedure > ECG criteria for STEMI Alerts: Please note that depending on the manufacturer of the > If the ECG monitor reading identifies a STEMI:
4.9.1.2.   Transmission of the ECG can dramatically reduce the door to balloon
time. Transmission shall be completed as soon as possible

[6] 430 VII.B.4 (STEMI Center Standards): STEMI Receiving Center Standards > Staffing Requirements
4. Registrar
Designate an individual to enter cases into the registry, pull
reports and assist with quality improvement and performance
indicator metrics.

[7] 700-A08 6.4 (Chest Pain - Suspected Cardiac Ischemia): Key Documentation Elements
6.4. Time of STEMI Alert notification to hospital

[8] 700-M09 2.1 (12-Lead Electrocardiogram): Definition
2.1. Electrocardiogram’s (ECGs) are utilized by prehospital personnel when a patient is
suspected of having abnormal cardiac function. The use of a 12-lead ECG is essential
to identify a patient experiencing an ST-elevation MI (STEMI).
